Subject: Production: sharp p99 surge + 502s since 07:45 PT

Hi team,

We're seeing a sudden spike in p99 latency and a growing number of 502s starting ~07:45 PT this morning. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on our side (same traffic polyfill), but your infra shows a few hundred 502s in the last 30m and p99 jumping from ~230ms to ~1.7s. The attached logs include the last 30 minutes of request traces and sample headers.

Immediate impact: our streaming endpoints intermittently cut connections; several customer retry loops are now amplifying traffic. We need a mitigation plan and ETA — we're on a customer call at 10:00 PT and need something actionable before then.

Subject: Re: Production: sharp p99 surge + 502s since 07:45 PT

Anoop / Vanessa — quick findings from initial triage against the logs you provided:

- Symptom set: concurrent long tail latencies + transient 502s when KV cache miss rate spikes.
- Root hypothesis: aggressive per-tenant TTL + small per-lane token budgets are causing KV cache churn; when a hot-prefix hits a cold path we see a cascade of prefetches that fill a single lane and block other lanes (head-of-line blocking). That creates temporary slot exhaustion followed by rapid evictions and re-prefetch, i.e., thrashing.

What I saw in the traces: several requests show identical prefix keys hitting different worker shards within milliseconds (signalling misrouting under the routing policy), then a cluster of prefetches with backpressure on the preferred lane. Prefetch queue depth increases, inflight KV fetches spike, and the runtime returns 502 when the request times out waiting for KV responses.

Immediate mitigations we can apply in the next 20–30 minutes (non-disruptive):
- Temporarily widen per-lane budget (increase tokens-per-lane) to avoid single-lane HOL collapse.
- Lower aggressive TTLs from 2s to 100–200ms for identified prefixes to reduce unnecessary retention.
- Turn on conservative routing to pin hot prefixes to a small set of shards to avoid misrouting-induced duplication.
- Throttle client burst windows for your tenant in the shared pool and divert excess to your dedicated pool if available.

I'll prepare a short rollout with exact CLI commands and a rollback plan. If we confirm dedicated-pool routing for the affected tenants we can route them there immediately and stop the noise while we investigate a long-term config fix.

Attachments: diagnostic-snippet.txt (inline snippet), suggested-config.diff

- Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
